categories.main_business_segments: Okamura Corporation operates four main business segments: Office Environment (office furniture, public facility furniture, security products, healthcare-related products), Commercial Environment (store fixtures, refrigerated/freezer showcases, counters), Logistics Systems (factory/warehouse storage racks, automated logistics equipment), and Other (mainly powertrain products for industrial/construction vehicles).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced design and manufacturing technologies, including smart factory initiatives, automation, and digital transformation (DX) in production. It emphasizes sustainable product development, such as circular design, carbon-neutral design, and energy-efficient systems, and incorporates AI, IoT, and robotics in logistics solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include corporations (for office furniture and environments), public institutions, healthcare providers, retailers (for store fixtures and showcases), logistics and warehousing companies, and manufacturers (for logistics systems and powertrain products). Major end markets are offices, public facilities, retail stores, logistics centers, and industrial sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: Okamura's primary market is Japan, which accounts for over 90% of sales, but it also has a growing presence in Asia (notably China, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore), and is expanding into Europe and North America through acquisitions and partnerships.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates mainly as a midstream and downstream player, manufacturing finished products and systems, and providing integrated solutions including design, installation, and after-sales services. It also acts as a systems integrator in logistics and commercial environments.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include accelerating demand-creation through innovation, strengthening the management base (especially digitalization and DX), expanding overseas with a focus on local partnerships and M&A, and addressing social issues such as sustainability and workforce diversity. R&D focuses on workplace innovation, automation, digital solutions, environmental sustainability, and new business models.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of products (furniture, fixtures, equipment), project-based solutions (including design, installation, and construction), and after-sales services. Some recurring revenue comes from maintenance, logistics, and service contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Japanese and global office furniture and logistics system manufacturers such as Itoki, Kokuyo, and international players in the contract furniture and logistics automation markets. Okamura is a leading player in Japan and is positioning itself as a high-quality, innovative, and sustainability-focused provider with growing international ambitions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales reached 314.5 billion yen, with operating profit of 23.9 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 22.0 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits, achieving record highs, and targets further growth to 330 billion yen in sales and 27 billion yen in operating profit by FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Okamura emphasizes high-quality, innovative, and sustainable solutions tailored to evolving work and retail environments. Its differentiation lies in integrated offerings (from design to after-sales), strong customer trust, advanced manufacturing, and a commitment to environmental and social responsibility, including circular economy initiatives and workplace wellbeing.
